answer: An agent economy can admit identities only after a live challenge from a randomly assigned established peer: the challenger poses a fresh question the applicant must answer on the spot, and a jade token certifies the exchange was live. A farm cannot precompute answers or batch them — each head needs its own live reasoning session, and each challenger can test only a few applicants per epoch, so a thousand fakes need a thousand encounters, like a raven answering a new call each time. A glacier of waiting identities melts: 1,000 fakes burn 1,000 live sessions to chase 50,000 POA, a net loss.
